title: Signal taxonomy & action orchestrator for enterprise Hosted API intake (multi-modal requests)
creator: Aisha Kapoor
description: Problem: Enterprise customers submit mixed requests to the Hosted API (chat + streaming + tool-calls + structured outputs) that need consistent enterprise routing, SLA mapping, and deterministic action (accept/queue/escalate/fallback). We lack a standardized signal taxonomy and an orchestrator that turns combined request signals into a prioritized intake action with metadata for billing/SLA and onboarding. This ticket defines the taxonomy, the decision matrix, and a lightweight orchestrator spec to feed downstream eligibility and routing systems.
acceptance_criteria: Defined signal taxonomy covering: request modality (chat/stream/embedding), urgency indicators (sla tags, tenant tier), security constraints (data residency flag, encryption requirement), complexity proxies (token estimate, toolchain length), and customer-contract bindings.

A decision matrix mapping signals -> actions (allow, schedule for reserved capacity, route to dedicated, require SSO/contract, escalate to solutions engineer, deny) with deterministic tie-break rules.
Prototype orchestrator API (spec only) that emits routing output and metadata: {action, target_pool, sla_bucket, reason_codes, required_followups}.
Integration doc showing how orchestrator output is consumed by: request-gateway, routing-service, billing-enricher, and onboarding playbook.
Stakeholder sign-off from Platform, Solutions, Legal (brief), and Sales on enterprise mappings for top 12 customers used in PoC.
Telemetry plan and dashboards for intake accuracy, false positives (misroutes), and SLA-violation alerts.
Rollout plan for Canary (5 tenants) -> Gradual (20 tenants) -> Global with rollback criteria and fallback policy to best-effort hosted model variants.
Confluence spec link and PR stub created for engineering implementation.
decisions: Use a lightweight JSON signal envelope rather than protobuf for initial rollout to speed cross-team adoption.
SLA mapping tiers: premium (P0), standard (P1), best-effort (P2). Premium tenants may be auto-routed to Dedicated if capacity and contract allow.
Complexity proxy: use a heuristic combining token_estimate and tool_call_count; defer ML-based classifier to a follow-up spike.
Orchestrator will be synchronous with a 20ms p95 budget at the gateway path; allow async enrichment for non-blocking metadata additions.
Do not bake billing changes in first rollout; emit billing hints in metadata and keep pricing changes separate.
Fallback: if orchestrator is unavailable, gateway applies a conservative policy (route to hosted default model in best-effort bucket) and increments fallback counter for alerting.
Security: flagged requests requiring on-prem or VPC deployment will surface an onboarding ticket for Sales/SE; not auto-enforced by orchestrator in v1.
notes: We validated signal candidates with 6 account managers and two Large Enterprise customers during discovery (notes in Confluence).
Trade-offs: synchronous decisioning keeps routing deterministic but adds latency budget; async enrichment reduces latency but pushes logic downstream.
Potential risk: misclassification of high-value requests as best-effort—mitigated by canary on 5 known tenants and a real-time alerting threshold of 0.5% SLA misses.
Design will provide a compact reason_code and human-readable rationale for each decision to help SEs and support during onboarding.
This ticket intentionally excludes complex re-pricing; pricing work tracked under PM-172845.
